Poland’s PM Tusk is now visiting the site of the incident, and says that two missiles violated Polish airspace during the night, but clarifies that the other one quickly crossed back into Ukraine .

title.en: How crypto miners are stealing power in Southeast Asia
title.zh: 东南亚加密货币矿工如何窃取电力

summary.en: Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime.
summary.zh: 在东南亚各地，非法加密货币矿工窃取大量电力，给国家电网带来压力，并暴露出与有组织犯罪的联系。

body.en:
Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime.

A raid in Malaysia last week exposed how  cryptocurrency mining is becoming entangled with electricity theft and organized crime across Southeast Asia.

In Malaysia's southern state of Johor, 71 cryptocurrency-mining machines had been running around the clock across four rented premises for about a month before police moved in.

During the raids on July 22 and 23, officers arrested three suspects and seized computers, routers and vehicles alongside equipment used to illegally mine Bitcoin . 

Johor police chief Ab Rahaman Arsad said the syndicate bypassed electricity meters, leading to an estimated €14,500 ($16,600) in losses in about a month, according to local media reports. The machines were thought to be generating between €17,200 and €21,500 in monthly revenue.

The case was relatively small by Malaysian standards. Between 2020 and 2025, national utility Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) identified almost 14,000 premises linked to electricity theft for cryptocurrency mining. Its cumulative losses reached around €1.1 billion.

Detected cases increased from 610 in 2018 to 2,397 in 2024, according to Malaysia's Energy Ministry, which has described illegal mining as a serious threat to public safety, economic stability and the national electricity system.

"In Malaysia, thousands of incidents have triggered investigations into illegal mining for cryptocurrency purposes," said Sonny Zulhuda, an associate professor at the International Islamic University Malaysia.

"This poses a huge problem for the security of electricity resources, economic sustainability, competition and revenue loss," Zulhuda told DW.

"Enforcement has been lagging behind due to a lack of legislative preparedness and limited agency capability in enforcement and investigation. This is unfortunate because Malaysia is fast developing its digital infrastructure."

Cryptocurrency mining is not inherently criminal. However, authorities are increasingly finding links between illegal crypto mining, online gambling, money laundering and Southeast Asia's industrial-scale cyber scam networks .

Last October, the United States and the UK sanctioned Cambodia -based Prince Group and associated companies, alleging that the network operated forced-labor scam compounds and laundered proceeds through cryptocurrencies and other assets.

US authorities also seized Bitcoin worth around $15 billion at the time from wallets whose private keys were held by Prince Group chairman Chen Zhi , describing the cryptocurrency as proceeds and instruments of fraud and money laundering.

title.en: Missile that left crater deep inside Poland was probably Russian - Polish PM
title.zh: 波兰总理：在波兰深处留下弹坑的导弹可能是俄罗斯制造的

summary.en: The missile left a 10m-wide (33ft) crater a short distance from the village of Tarnawa Kolonia, about 100km from the border with Ukraine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has said an object that crashed into a field in eastern Poland in the early hours of Thursday was probably a Russian missile.

The unidentified object caused a 10m-wide (33ft) crater a short distance from the village of Tarnawa Kolonia, 92km (57 miles) from the border with Ukraine during a large-scale Russian attack on the cities of Lviv, Kyiv and near Kryvyhi Rih.

Tusk said initially that "all the indications" were that the missile that violated Polish airspace was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, during a specially convened meeting in the eastern city of Lublin.

He then went to the site of the incident and said that according to military experts the majority of "recovered fragments point to it being a Russian Kh-101 missile".

Although no casualties had been reported in Thursday's incident near Tarnawa Kolonia, the Polish prime minister made clear it was being taken very seriously.

There was no immediate threat as it had not landed in a built-up area, he said, adding that "we were prepared to shoot it down if had continued its flight".

Nato said it was in close contact with Polish authorities and the Supreme Allied Commander in Europe, Gen Alexus G Grynkewich, said the Western defensive alliance would "continue to take all necessary measures to defend Nato territory".

Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said about 20 objects were seen close to Polish airspace overnight and pyrotechnical analysis was being carried out.

Ukraine's acting Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha had earlier declared definitively that a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile had "crossed into Poland as part of Russia's massive strike against Ukraine, violating Nato airspace".

Tusk said he was in contact with fellow European leaders and the head of the European Council António Costa said Russia's "massive combined strike against Ukraine" had underlined again that "Russia's aggression is a threat to the security as a whole".

At least eight people died and dozens more were wounded across Ukraine, including six members of one family in a village near Kryvyih Rih. Dozens more were wounded in Lviv, not far from Ukraine's western border with Poland.

A number of Russian drones and one unarmed Russian missile have landed in Poland since Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine began in February 2022.

Two Polish farmers were killed by a missile that landed just over the border from Ukraine in November 2022, but that was believed to have been a Ukrainian air defence missile responding to a Russian attack.

Poland's military detected the object at about 03:40 on Thursday (01:40 GMT) and sent an F-16 fighter jet to intercept it before it disappeared minutes later from radar systems. A military helicopter was then sent to search the area.

body.zh: 波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克表示，周四凌晨坠入波兰东部田野的一个物体可能是一枚俄罗斯导弹。 在俄罗斯对利沃夫、基辅和克利维希里赫附近城市进行大规模袭击时，这个不明物体在距乌克兰边境 92 公里（57 英里）的 Tarnawa Kolonia 村附近造成了一个 10m 宽（33 英尺）的弹坑。 图斯克在东部城市卢布林举行的一次特别会议上最初表示，“所有迹象”都表明，侵犯波兰领空的导弹是俄罗斯 Kh-101 巡航导弹。 随后他前往事发地点并表示，根据军事专家的说法，大多数“回收的碎片表明这是一枚俄罗斯 Kh-101 导弹”。 尽管周四塔尔纳瓦科洛尼亚附近的事件没有造成人员伤亡，但波兰总理明确表示正在非常严肃地对待这起事件。 他说，由于它没有降落在建筑区，所以没有立即构成威胁，并补充说，“如果它继续飞行，我们准备将其击落”。 北约表示，它正在与波兰当局保持密切联系，欧​​洲盟军最高指挥官亚历克苏斯·G·格林克维奇将军表示，西方防御联盟将“继续采取一切必要措施保卫北约领土”。 波兰国防部长瓦迪斯瓦夫·科西尼亚克-卡米什表示，夜间在波兰领空附近发现了约20个物体，目前正在进行烟火分析。 乌克兰代理外交部长安德烈·西比哈早些时候明确宣布，一枚俄罗斯Kh-101巡航导弹“作为俄罗斯对乌克兰大规模打击的一部分进入波兰，侵犯了北约领空”。 图斯克表示，他正在与其他欧洲领导人保持联系，欧洲理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔表示，俄罗斯“对乌克兰的大规模联合打击”再次强调“俄罗斯的侵略是对整个安全的威胁”。 乌克兰各地至少有八人死亡，数十人受伤，其中包括克里沃罗格附近一个村庄的一个家庭的六名成员。利沃夫距乌克兰西部与波兰边境不远，另有数十人受伤。 自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯在乌克兰全面战争开始以来，多架俄罗斯无人机和一枚非武装俄罗斯导弹已降落在波兰。 2022 年 11 月，一枚导弹落在乌克兰边境上空，两名波兰农民被炸死，但据信那是乌克兰防空导弹对俄罗斯袭击的回应。 波兰军方于周四凌晨 3 点 40 分（格林威治标准时间 01 点 40 分）左右发现了该物体，并派出一架 F-16 战斗机进行拦截，几分钟后该物体从雷达系统中消失。随后派出一架军用直升机前往该地区进行搜索。 空袭...

summary.en: Strong winds have fanned the flames in the Rethymno region as wildfires continue to ravage the Greek island.

body.en:
Thousands of people have been evacuated on the Greek island of Crete as wildfires fanned by strong winds menace tourist resorts and villages.

Two firefighters died on the island on Wednesday when they became trapped while tackling a fire near Krya Vrysi in the Rethymno region. A third firefighter died on the Greek mainland, near the port town of Gytheio in the Peloponnese.

As gusts reached 125km/h (77mph) on the island, around 8,000 people were evacuated from their homes overnight but were later allowed to return.

Several fires have continued to burn in Spain and Portugal, although Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared an end to the national emergency for wildfires in the Ávila and Madrid regions.

In south-west France some residents have been able to return to their homes after a major wildfire in the Gironde region.

The fire raging in Crete broke out in the Rethymno region on Wednesday and has since spread rapidly, destroying homes and agricultural land. It remains one of the biggest fires currently active on the island and is still burning out of control.

There was no clear picture of the destruction so far, Rethymno's deputy regional governor Maria Lioni said, adding that containing the fire was the main priority.

Lioni described Wednesday as a "dark day" for the region and said gusts overnight reached up to 11 on the Beaufort scale - a wind force categorised as "violent" - fanning the flames and hampering containment efforts.

"It was frightening," British tourist Peter Wood told news agency Reuters the shelter. "We could see the flames in the hills above the village, and the police and firefighters were just telling everyone to leave straight away."

The large fire occurs during one of Crete's busiest months for tourism. Hundreds of firefighters have been deployed to the region to battle the blaze.

Hellenic Fire Service chief Theodoros Vagias expressed his condolences for the two firefighters who died on Wednesday, naming them as 58-year-old Emmanouil Stratidakis and Pantelis Diamantakis, 25.

Meanwhile, wildfires have erupted in the north-western Spanish provinces of Zamora and León, not far from the border with Portugal, with more than 1,000 people evacuated.

Five people were injured in a fire in the eastern town of Valpaços in Portugal, according to local reports.

A major fire that consumed an area in excess of 66,000 hectares to the west of the Spanish capital, Madrid, and caused tens of thousands of people to be evacuated has stopped spreading, allowing some residents to return home.

As he ended the national emergency in the area, Pedro Sánchez urged "extreme caution" during the fourth heatwave of the summer in Spain.

title.en: Crete wildfires cause evacuations and firefighter deaths
title.zh: 克里特岛野火导致疏散和消防员死亡

summary.en: Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.

Greek firefighters battled deadly wildfires on the island of Crete for a second day on Thursday as strong winds made it difficult to contain the flames.

Two firefighters were killed while responding to fires on the island, while a third died fighting a separate blaze on the Greek mainland.

Fires advancing across southwestern Crete forced several villages in the Rethymno region to be evacuated. Flames also neared the popular resort town of Agia Galini on the island's southern coast, pushing tourists to leave. 

In total, roughly 8,000 people were evacuated, the island's deputy governor Maria Lioni said.

The fires have already destroyed large areas of farmland, including olive groves, as well as residential homes.

Firefighters have struggled to contain the blazes because of strong and constantly shifting winds, which have reached speeds of up to 102 kilometers (63 miles) per hour.

As a result, emergency services said aircraft used to drop water on the fires were severely limited or could not be deployed at all.

"Unfortunately there is no improvement, and the latest information ​indicates that winds will increase later in the day," Giorgos Tsapakos, the deputy regional governor for civil protection on Crete, told Greek television.

Two firefighters died combating the flames in Crete after being trapped on a mountain road, losing their bearings as smoke enveloped them. A third firefighter collapsed and died while on duty near Gytheio on the Southern end of the Peloponnese peninsula.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis paid tribute to the fallen firefighters on Wednesday, acknowledging the "new harsh reality” they face each year, as wildfires worsen. 

Greece , like other Southern European countries, is facing a heightened risk of wildfires as climate change exacerbates droughts, high temperatures and extreme winds  which create ideal conditions for blazes.

In France and Spain, meanwhile, firefighting efforts on Thursday seemed to be turning a corner.

In France, authorities permitted the return of 84,000 evacuees forced out by a wildfire near the southwestern city of Bordeaux, as cooler temperatures and rain offered some respite. The fire had led to around 220,000 people being displaced .

In Spain, too, wildfires threatening Madrid were abating, as authorities reported "almost no flames" left.

body.en:
Australia's eSafety Commissioner has announced legal action against messaging app Telegram for its failure to remove terrorist content, just one day after Russia charged the app's founder with aiding Ukrainian spies to co-ordinate domestic terrorist attacks.

eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant told reporters on Thursday that Telegram continued to host videos linked to the Christchurch mosque shootings and executions by the self-proclaimed Islamic State group, both illegal and restricted Class 1 content in Australia.

Grant said the app has "a fundamental responsibility to take reasonable steps to prevent the hosting, sharing and amplification of this harmful material".

Telegram, based in the United Arab Emirates, is one of the world's largest messaging platforms with more than one billion active users worldwide. It is not included in Australia's youth social media ban .

Grant said her agency first began compliance talks with the digital platform in March 2024. Despite Telegram's engagement, Grant said the platform continued to host harmful content.

"We allege that this content remained publicly accessible on the service long after Telegram had been put on notice by user reports," she said.

The maximum penalty for non-compliance is $54.4 million; however, Grant told the press that the appropriate penalty was a "matter for the court".

In 2025, Telegram was fined $957,780 by the eSafety Commissioner for delays in reporting the steps the platform has taken to minimise terrorism and child abuse material.

On Wednesday, Russia said it had charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging the app was being used by Ukrainian spies to organise attacks inside Russia.

In response, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of the Russian-born billionaire making an obscene gesture with his middle finger.

The charges, announced by Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB), marked the culmination of a long investigation against Dubai-based Durov and Telegram.

Russia has effectively throttled the service as part of a wider campaign to cut off access to foreign tech platforms and tighten control over the internet.

Russians can now access Telegram only via a virtual private network to encrypt traffic and conceal their location. Yet state bodies including the Kremlin and the defence ministry continue to post to it daily.

The app has been described as a "virtual battlefield" in the war between Russia and Ukraine, where it is used by officials, soldiers and influential bloggers on both sides.

summary.zh: 日本发生地震，一座永旺购物中心倒塌，造成13人死亡，救援人员正在紧急搜寻幸存者。

body.en:
At least 17 people have died after a major earthquake struck Japan, local authorities said on Thursday in a revised toll two days after the tremor.

The Kumamoto disaster management office's latest tally put fatalities at 17 and the number of those without vital signs at six, with five more in critical condition.

Rescuers have continued to battle through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall searching for any trapped survivors.

A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people.

The earthquake caused widespread damage on the island of Kyushu, flattening homes, triggering fires and leaving tens of thousands of residents without power and water.

Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.

"The cause is still being investigated, but it's likely that gas caused it," fellow Aeon executive Keiji Ohno told a news conference where he and others bowed in apology.

Five people were also confirmed killed, and four others were unaccounted for at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, where part of a red-and-white smokestack collapsed, a government official told reporters from the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency.

Government spokesman Minoru Kihara said that as of early Wednesday, more than 9,000 people had sought refuge in 506 shelters across three regions of Kyushu Island.

Around 130 police, 450 firefighters and 170 military personnel were involved in the rescue operation at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto, he said.

Some stunned locals said the quake was the biggest they had felt in their lifetimes, measuring at the top of Japan's seven-level shindo scale of shakiness.

"It was the strongest quake I ever experienced," Kanzo Matsumoto, 73, the operator of a luxury onsen hot spring inn in Yatsushiro, told AFP.

Japan's Geospatial Information Authority said some ground surfaces were displaced by up to 87 centimetres during the quake, Jiji Press reported.

Tokito Kitagawa, 21, pulled over at a convenience store when the quake struck as he was travelling in Kumamoto on his motorcycle.

"There was a sudden big noise," Kitagawa told AFP. "I couldn't stay standing. I had to crouch down. Then all the cup noodles fell all over me on the floor."

body.zh: 星期三，一场强烈地震造成至少 13 人死亡，救援人员在日本一家购物中心的废墟中奋力搜寻被困的幸存者。 周二，熊本西南部地区发生 7.1 级地震，大约 50 分钟后，购物中心发生了大规模爆炸，该地区在 2016 年的两次地震中造成近 300 人死亡。 周二的地震对九州岛造成了大范围的破坏，房屋被夷为平地，引发火灾，导致数万居民断电断水。 商场运营商永旺集团总裁吉田昭夫表示，鹿岛镇的这家设施中有三人死亡，预计还有一人死亡，另外三人失踪。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 永旺公司高管大野敬二在新闻发布会上表示：“原因仍在调查中，但很可能是气体造成的。”他和其他人在新闻发布会上鞠躬致歉。 一名政府官员告诉法新社记者，八代市日本造纸工业工厂的红白烟囱部分倒塌，造成五人死亡，另外四人下落不明。 日本首相高市早苗在东京宣布造成 13 人死亡，并表示正在“与时间赛跑”，以帮助受影响的人们，“已确认造成广泛损失，包括人员伤亡、建筑物倒塌、火灾和道路损坏”。 政府发言人 Minoru Kihara 表示，截至周三早些时候，已有 9000 多人在九州岛三个地区的 506 个避难所寻求庇护。 他说，大约 130 名警察、450 名消防员和 170 名军事人员参与了熊本永旺购物中心的救援行动。 一些震惊的当地人表示，这次地震是他们一生中感受到的最大地震，达到了日本七级震级的最高级别。 八代市一家豪华温泉旅馆的经营者、73 岁的松本勘三 (Kanzo Matsumoto) 告诉法新社：“这是我经历过的最强烈的地震。” 据时事通讯社报道，日本地理空间信息管理局表示，地震中一些地面位移达 87 厘米。 地震发生时，21 岁的喜多川时人 (Tokito Kitakawa) 骑着摩托车在熊本旅行，他在一家便利店停车。 喜多川告诉法新社：“突然传来一声巨响。” “我无法站着，只能蹲下。然后所有的杯面都掉到了地板上。” X 上的一位自称在商场内工作的用户讲述了地震发生后的情景。 账号为“Palan”的用户表示，工作人员已将顾客引导到外面，然后一些员工回去拿东西。

reflection.en: In the wake of such sudden devastation, our hearts go out to those affected and the tireless rescuers. Even amidst the chaos and uncertainty, we can find solace in knowing that Yahweh is a present help in times of trouble, offering strength and refuge.
reflection.zh: 面对突如其来的灾难，我们的心与受灾者和不懈的救援人员同在。即使在混乱和不确定中，我们也能在雅伟是患难中随时的帮助、赐予力量和避难所的真理中找到慰藉。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

body.en: There is no point competing in isolation. Like the steam engine, the harnessing of electricity and the internet before it, it has the potential to transform how we work, live and interact. How can AI remain safe, accountable and under human control ? How should its development be governed? How can its benefits be shared more widely? Continue reading...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to hope, endurance, and faithful rebuilding. Romans 12:12 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with steady hope and perseverance, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到盼望、忍耐与重建。Romans 12:12提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以坚定盼望与忍耐来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: The Chinese robot army transforming the UK's retail industry
title.zh: 改变英国零售业的中国机器人大军

summary.en: Britain's retail sector is increasingly adopting robotics from Chinese firms to combat low productivity and labor shortages.
summary.zh: 英国零售业正日益采用中国机器人公司的技术，以应对生产力低下和劳动力短缺的问题。

body.en:
Every time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.

Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.

At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.

Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.

By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.

Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.

Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.

The UK has struggled with weak productivity growth for more than a decade, and economists say wider adoption of robotics will be essential if businesses are to become more efficient.

In its 2026 report SME Technology Adoption in the United Kingdom, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said technologies like robotics would be key to improving productivity.

According to the OECD, Britain's low adoption of robotics is "surprising" given its manufacturing heritage, noting that while UK firms have embraced mature digital technologies, they lag behind in robotics and automation.

That presents an opportunity for companies such as Geek+. The UK has one of Europe's largest e-commerce and logistics sectors, but many warehouses are still in the early stages of automation.

Britain has already become Geek+'s biggest European market, with UK partner MotionTech deploying more than 2,000 robots across 10 warehouse sites.

"Customers want fast deployable solutions," says Barry Pemberton, Account Director at MotionTech. "They want high volume, high storage, fast picking... ultimately on a smaller footprint with a reduced headcount."

"We seem to have a very big shortage of labour in the UK at the moment. These technologies are really important to keep businesses thriving and meet demand."

The Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents almost 6 million UK workers, says robotics should be used to raise productivity and improve jobs, rather than simply cut labour costs.

In its response to the government's consultation on a new AI and innovation strategy, it urged ministers to ensure workers are involved in decisions about automation...

reflection.en: As robotics transform industries and redefine human roles, we are invited to consider the deeper purpose of our work. Colossians 3:23 reminds us to approach every task with diligence and integrity, working heartily as for Yahweh. This perspective elevates our labor beyond mere economic output, imbuing it with lasting meaning and dignity.
reflection.zh: 随着机器人技术改变行业并重新定义人类的角色，我们被邀请思考我们工作的更深层目的。歌罗西书3:23提醒我们，要以勤奋和正直的态度对待每一项任务，如同为雅伟而做。这种视角将我们的劳动提升到超越单纯经济产出的层面，赋予其持久的意义和尊严。

title.en: US bans Chinese and foreign-made humanoid robots
title.zh: 美国禁止中国及外国制造的仿人机器人

summary.en: The Trump administration has prohibited the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. This ban could potentially escalate diplomatic tensions with China.
summary.zh: 特朗普政府以国家安全为由，禁止进口美国以外制造的仿人机器人和四足机器人。这项禁令可能会加剧与中国的外交紧张关系。

body.en:
The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

The United States has announced a ban on the import of foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in a move which will likely exclude Chinese manufacturers from the US market and could strain tensions between Washington and Beijing .

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Tuesday that "advanced robotic devices" produced abroad posed national and cyber security risks to the United States.

The decision was based on findings from a White House task force which concluded that foreign-built robots could create "a cybersecurity risk that threatens the security of critical infrastructure" and "the safety and security" of US residents.

The FCC defines the relevant mobile robots as devices weighing more than two kilograms that use sensors, network connectivity and software to achieve autonomous navigation, including the avoidance of obstacles.

The market for humanoid and quadruped (also known as four-legged "robot dogs") is seen as a major international growth area, with US and Chinese companies competing to develop the technology.

And China has a clear lead, with analysts at Barclays estimating that Chinese-made humanoid robots account for around 85% of the global market share. Morgan Stanley experts predict that China's humanoid robot market could be worth $15 billion (€13.2 billion) by 2030.

"Chinese manufacturers have been scaling production and reducing costs faster than most overseas competitors," Morningstar analyst Kangyuxiao Li told the Associated Press .

In the US, firms such as Figure AI are already deploying humanoid robots on production lines, while tech giant Tesla plans to begin production of its "Optimus" robot this year.

Currently, however, US robot exports remain in their hundreds while Unitree and AGIBOT, two of China's biggest advanced robotics companies, each shipped more than 5,000 humanoid robots in 2025 alone, according to the technology research and advisory group Omdia.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the ban was also aimed at "secur[ing] America's critical supply chains."

But Li said the measures would not "materially slow China's overall humanoid development, given the size of its domestic manufacturing base and opportunities in other export markets."

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

body.en: New research linking the issue to Parkinson’s disease adds to the evidence of serious health repercussions from traffic volume and other sources The roar of late-night traffic is not just annoying for those trying to sleep. The European Environment Agency reported last year that more than 110 million people across the continent suffer high levels of health-damaging noise pollution, with physiological stress and sleep disturbance leading to 66,000 early deaths annually as well as heart disease, diabetes and depression. title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

body.en:
Australia celebrates the value of mateship, but distrust between the population has grown to the highest level reported this decade.

A survey of over 3,500 people, conducted by the Australian National University in June, suggests Australians trust each other less than they did during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Professor Nicholas Biddle, head of ANU's School of Politics and International Relations, said some of the findings were concerning.

"Worryingly, interpersonal trust among Australians has fallen to 5.32 on a scale of 0 to 10 — the lowest value recorded in ANUpoll during the 2020s,'' he said.

"This sits below the pre-COVID value of 5.53 recorded in October 2019 and reverses the increase in trust observed during the pandemic."

Researchers asked participants three questions: whether they believed most people could be trusted, whether someone would take advantage of them if given the chance, and whether people are generally helpful or selfish in their choices.

While the results for all three indicated declining trust, the most dramatic decrease was in belief that others can be trusted, Biddle said.

He also noted that trust remains strongest among "older Australians, degree holders and the employed".

The findings follow data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ General Social Survey from 2025 that found half of Australians felt others could be trusted — compared to 61 per cent in 2020.

Similarly, Scanlon Foundation Research Institute CEO Anthea Hancocks said the findings reflected those of her organisation.

"People who are employed each day or very often are going to a workplace where there are other people working towards a similar goal — and they're getting paid," she explained.

"That gives you a greater sense of self-worth that you may not necessarily have if you're unemployed."

She suggested that higher trust among older Australians may be related to her organisation's findings that this cohort had "a higher sense of belonging than any other age group".

"That's generally because they know the world in which they're living; they're quite comfortable with their circumstances," she said.

"They know what they are and have an understanding of what the future holds. Unlike young people, whose sense of belonging is way below average."

The ANUpoll also found that between March and June of 2026, life satisfaction in Australia plateaued at 6.22 out of 10.

Over the same period, the proportion of those who experienced difficult or very difficult levels of financial stress decreased slightly from 34.9 per cent in March to 33 per cent in June.

body.en:
Ashleigh Middleton has spent months campaigning to keep a drug that's holding her cancer at bay on Australian shelves.

Now she's won — but says the uncertainty surrounding long-term access hasn't gone away.

The 31-year-old breast cancer patient was shocked when it was announced in April that Zoladex — a monthly implant used to suppress hormones in women with hormone-positive breast cancer as well as a range of other conditions affecting women — would be pulled from the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) and no longer supplied through its usual distribution pathway from 1 November.

The decision, made by the drug's manufacturer, AstraZeneca, prompted concern among patients and clinicians who questioned how those who rely on the treatment would access an alternative and whether suitable substitutes would be available for all conditions the implant is used to treat.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Angered by the move and worried about the precedent it could set for other medications, Middleton started a change.org petition, calling on AstraZeneca to reverse the decision and urging the federal government and the Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee to secure PBS-listed alternatives.

The company now says it will provide the monthly implant free of charge to patients who have no suitable alternative, with no end date listed — a shift from its earlier plan to provide six months of free access while patients transitioned to other arrangements.

Asked whether AstraZeneca could guarantee the medication would remain available, a spokesperson told SBS News: "The Zoladex Continuity Program is not a time-bound program."

For Middleton, it's a win worth celebrating — but not one that has settled her nerves.

"It's a really, really good step in the right direction, but it's definitely not all the way there," she tells SBS News.

"But I think AstraZeneca have recognised it was probably a bad decision on their part, so at least putting a little something extra in there, saying it's indefinitely going to be available and that there's no cut-off time, I think is a positive," Middleton says.

Two weeks on from that announcement, with November fast approaching, those affected are left with a mix of celebration, confusion and ongoing concern about what access will look like in practice.

While many people may not have heard of Zoladex, its 3.6mg implant has become a lifeline for many of the patients who rely on it.

It's prescribed to suppress hormones in premenopausal women with hormone-positive breast cancer, helping reduce the risk of recurrence by suppressing ovarian hormone production.

title.en: What is Garma Festival? Australia's biggest Indigenous gathering returns for 2026
title.zh: 什么是加尔马节？澳大利亚最大的原住民聚会将于2026年回归

summary.en: The annual Garma Festival, Australia's largest Indigenous gathering, is set to return this weekend on Yolŋu Country, celebrating Indigenous culture.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚最大的原住民聚会——一年一度的加尔马节将于本周末在约尔古地区举行，庆祝原住民文化。

body.en:
Thousands of people will travel to north-east Arnhem Land this week as the Garma Festival returns to Yolŋu Country for four days of ceremony, culture and national conversation.

Held on Gumatj Country in the Northern Territory, Garma remains Australia's largest Indigenous cultural gathering .

This year marks more than a quarter of a century since it started as a small community gathering, and will run from 31 July until 3 August.

Each year it brings together Yolŋu Elders, artists, young people, political leaders, academics, business representatives and visitors from across the country.

It is a place where ancient ceremony sits alongside some of Australia's biggest conversations about First Nations policy.

This year, those discussions will unfold without Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, despite his commitment last year to attend every Garma while serving as prime minister.

Hosted by the Yothu Yindi Foundation since 1999, Garma was established to celebrate and strengthen Yolŋu culture while creating a place where Aboriginal knowledge, leadership and ideas could be shared with the broader Australian community.

The word Garma comes from Yolŋu Matha and refers to a meeting place where different ideas come together through a process of two-way learning.

That philosophy remains central to the festival today. While Garma is grounded in Yolŋu ceremony and tradition, it has also become one of Australia's most influential forums for discussion on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander affairs.

Each year, governments, community organisations, academics and industry leaders travel to Arnhem Land to listen, learn and engage directly with Yolŋu leaders on Country.

Garma is held at Gulkula, a sacred ceremonial site on Gumatj Country near Nhulunbuy in north-east Arnhem Land.

Surrounded by stringybark forest and overlooking the Gulf of Carpentaria, Gulkula has been a place of ceremony and renewal for generations.

According to Yolŋu tradition, it is where the ancestor Ganbulapula introduced the yidaki into Yolŋu life, making it one of the region's most culturally significant places.

Unlike many conferences, Garma is held on Yolŋu Country and led on Yolŋu terms.

Rather than Aboriginal leaders travelling to Canberra, governments, institutions and organisations travel to Arnhem Land, placing First Nations culture, knowledge and authority at the centre of the national conversation.

Visitors camp on Country throughout the four-day festival and are asked to observe cultural protocols guided by their Yolŋu hosts.

title.en: There's something else Neil the seal wrecked in Tasmania — the council's bank account
title.zh: 海豹尼尔在塔斯马尼亚还毁坏了一些东西——议会的银行账户

summary.en: The social media sensation, famous for loathing bollards, has returned to the ocean for another year.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Neil the seal captures hearts and global attention during his visits to Tasmania, but his most recent stay racked up a bill of more than $36,000.

The five-year-old elephant seal hauls out twice a year to rest and moult in the island state's south-east, where he was born.

His antics, including crushing bollards and fences, and lounging on quiet beach-side streets, have drawn millions of views on social media.

In June, wildlife authorities issued a blunt public statement, urging people to keep their distance or risk "loving Neil to death".

His 15-day stay at Seven Mile Beach cost the local Clarence City Council a total of $31,540.53 — the majority relating to staffing and labour.

There is also a repair bill for one flattened street sign, 10 knocked-over bollards and one crushed fence, costing council $1,297.70 in materials.

Staff, including a 24-hour security presence, spent 275.5 hours managing traffic and crowds and repairing damage.

"Neil is a wild animal, and the overexposure and constant public attention he received could have led to a more dramatic outcome," Blomeley said.

"Wherever he decides to come ashore next, I hope he is given the space and time he needs."

Right-to-information documents obtained by the ABC show that Tasmania's natural resources and environment department has spent more than $45,000 managing Neil's four haul-outs in 2025 and 2026.

Neil's June haul-out cost the department $4,794, but it was still calculating the full price tag.

Neil, who currently weighs one tonne, safely returned to sea in early July and is expected to come back to Tasmania later in the year once he's done feeding in the Southern Ocean.

He was rescued by wildlife authorities after being born on a beach in southern Tasmania.

Experts have said his "jousting" with posts and other objects is natural behaviour, and something seals of his age usually do with each other.

There were once southern elephant seals in Tasmania, but they were wiped out by hunting in the early 1800s.

"Neil is potentially one of the first southern elephant seal pups to be born back in Tasmania," department wildlife expert Kris Carlyon has said.

"Regardless of the resource burden and the challenges that Neil throws, we're pleased to see him."

title.en: ACMA sues Optus over 2025 network outage and failed Triple Zero calls

summary.en: The Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) has initiated legal proceedings against telecommunications company Optus. This action follows a significant network outage in 2025 that prevented emergency Triple Zero calls from connecting, an issue similar to one experienced weeks prior with another provider,...
summary.zh: 澳大利亚通信和媒体管理局（ACMA）已对电信公司Optus提起法律诉讼。此前，Optus在2025年发生了一次大规模网络中断，导致紧急三零电话无法接通，这与几周前另一家供应商Telstra也曾出现类似问题。

body.en:
Australia's second-largest telco is facing legal action over a major network failure that caused a widespread Triple Zero outage.

The Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) alleges Optus breached two legal obligations more than 1,000 times during the outage on 18 September, 2025.

Access to emergency call services was essential to protect the public, the regulator's chair Nerida O'Loughlin said.

"Australians rightly expect that when they call Triple Zero, their call will connect," she said in a statement on Thursday.

"The circumstances of this outage meant that did not reliably occur, leaving people unable to connect to potentially life-saving services.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Giving access to the emergency call service is not optional; it is a fundamental legal obligation, and the most important public safety responsibility telecommunications providers have."

Optus failed to give customers who made Triple Zero calls access to the emergency call service and to ensure those calls were carried appropriately , the regulator alleged.

The proceedings against the Singaporean-owned company announced on Thursday will be heard in the Federal Court.

The legal action follows the massive outage which went for almost 14 hours and impacted 600 calls, with 455 failing to connect.

An independent review, released by Optus in December, found there were at least 10 mistakes by the company and its contractor Nokia during an upgrade.

It took Optus and Nokia 13 hours to understand the problem, with an Optus call centre not escalating early concerns from five people who said their Triple Zero calls weren't working, the report by experienced executive Kerry Schott found.

The watchdog has previously taken action against the telco following another Triple Zero outage in November 2023.

The action resulted in Singtel Optus subsidiaries, including Optus Mobile, paying more than $12 million in infringement notice penalties for breaches relating to emergency calls.
